# grid.View owns the selection model and grid.Body carries none: null selects nothing, RowModel is the View's default

## Context

A consumer that renders a designed list through `Neo.grid.Container` (a single component column, no header, cards as cells — the Fleet Manager's memories registers, neomjs/neo-agent-institution#131; the mailbox and catch-up surfaces follow the same law) has no selection semantics: its only act is a click inside the card. The engine still marks the clicked row: `grid.Body#beforeSetSelectionModel` runs `ClassSystemUtil.beforeSetInstance(value, RowModel)`, and `beforeSetInstance` instantiates the default class for a falsy value — so the body's `selectionModel_: null` default becomes a `RowModel` at construction, `grid.Container#applyViewSelectionModel(me.view.selectionModel || me.body?.selectionModel)` hoists it to the `grid.View`, and every click paints `.neo-selected`. Measured 2026-09-12 on the memories register at pin dev@28e56e1543 (the Institution's Neural Link witness: the clicked row's `neo-selected` is `true` with no selection model declared anywhere by the consumer).

## The Problem

There is no way to say "this grid selects nothing", and the reason is structural: the selection model is still CONFIGURED on `grid.Body`, while the multi-body design (#9486, phase #9492; the View-owned single instance of #12758 / PR #12784) says the View owns selection and the bodies are render/event delegates. The body-level config survived that refactor as a forwarding seam — `body.selectionModel` hoists to the View, the locked bodies are created with `selectionModel: null` "so they do not clone", which the body defaults to a transient `RowModel` each (measured 2026-09-13: two extra instances per grid on dev@5dc6b80fef), and `BaseModel.getActivePeers()` still fans row updates out to peers that no longer exist. Every attempt to express "none" at the body level is a sentinel on the wrong owner (PR #18656, drafted and superseded: `false` on the body — the direction the maintainer ruled out on 2026-09-13: *a VIEW is in charge of selections, not bodies; grid bodies should not get selection models at all*).

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/View.mjs` — `selectionModel_: null` (~75) with `beforeSetSelectionModel` keeping a falsy value and `afterSetSelectionModel` → `value?.register(this)`: the View already owns the instance's lifecycle (destroy on swap, registration, keyboard keys). The static config declares `keys` before `selectionModel_`, so a model registered at construction finds the key-navigation carrier.
- `src/grid/Body.mjs` — `selectionModel_: null` (~222) + `beforeSetSelectionModel` (instantiates the default) + `afterSetSelectionModel` (forwards a post-construction swap up); readers: the `selectedCells` / `selectedRows` getters, `onStoreRecordChange`, `toJSON`; `src/grid/Row.mjs` destructures `selectionModel` / `selectedCells` off the body for the paint.
- `src/grid/Container.mjs` — creates the View with a fixed config (`construct`, ~284: no consumer seam), the locked bodies with `selectionModel: null` (849, 874), and hoists in `createOrUpdateSubGrids` → `applyViewSelectionModel` (~904–934).
- `src/selection/grid/BaseModel.mjs` — `getActivePeers()` (~252) reads `container.bodyStart?.selectionModel` … and seven call sites fan `updateRows` out to peers (`ColumnModel.mjs:79` too) — dead since the single instance, still executed.
- Consumers configure through the body: `body: {selectionModel: X}` (`examples/grid/container`, `examples/grid/cellEditing`, `apps/email/view/MainView.mjs`), `grid.body.selectionModel = X` (`examples/grid/bigData`, `examples/grid/treeBigData` controls), `setProperties(gridId, {'body.selectionModel': …})` (`test/playwright/e2e/grid/SelectionMultiBody.spec.mjs`, `GridViewFocus.spec.mjs`); the guides `learn/guides/datahandling/Grids.md:589` and `learn/guides/fundamentals/InstanceLifecycle.md:268–275` teach the body as the owner.

## The Fix

Complete the View ownership. The View is the only place a selection model is configured, instantiated, registered and destroyed; the bodies carry none.

1. **`grid.View`** — `selectionModel_` defaults to the `RowModel` class (the default lives with the owner); `null` means NONE — no instance, no row ever marked, no selection handler; a config or instance is the explicit model. `beforeSetSelectionModel` keeps normalizing every falsy value to `null`.
2. **`grid.Container`** — a `viewConfig` (plain object, the `…Config` idiom) merged into the View's creation is the consumer seam: `viewConfig: {selectionModel: null}` / `{selectionModel: {module: CellModel}}`; `grid.view.selectionModel = X` is the dynamic write. `applyViewSelectionModel` and the locked bodies' `selectionModel` lines are deleted — there is nothing to hoist.
3. **`grid.Body`** — `selectionModel_`, its two hooks, `selectedRecordField` and the `selectedCells` / `selectedRows` readers are deleted. A body exposes no model — there is no accessor; a setter throws the migration pointer, so a leftover `body: {selectionModel: …}` fails loudly at construction instead of silently defaulting. `Row` paints the View's projected selection (`view.selectedRows` / `view.selectedCells`) and never mutates it; `Body#onStoreRecordChange` only repaints the row it renders.
4. **The selection policy leaves the render delegates.** The View owns `selectedRecordField` and follows the store once (`bindStore`, from `onConstructed` and from `grid.Container#afterSetStore` on a store swap): records flagged in the data are adopted through the model's own `selectRow` when the store binds or loads — the model's policy applies, `singleSelect` included — and a flag change reaches the model exactly once, however many bodies render the record. `View#createViewData` re-projects the bodies for the column-selecting models, which call it on the View they register with; `View#destroy` retires the model and the store listeners. The flag is followed under the row-selecting models — `RowModel` and the combined `CellRowModel` / `CellColumnRowModel`, the set the old `Body#selectedRows` getter served (`ntype` containing `row`) — through one predicate, `View#rowSelectionModel`, that the paint getters share; a cell or column model leaves a record's flag alone.
5. **`selection/grid/BaseModel`** — `getActivePeers()` and its fan-out call sites (and `ColumnModel`'s) are deleted: one instance spans all bodies through `updateRows` already.
6. **Consumers and guides** — the three `body: {selectionModel}` configs move to `viewConfig`, the two controls and the two e2e specs write `view.selectionModel`, the unit spec drops the body-level `selectionModel: null`, the two guides name the View as the owner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 `viewConfig: {selectionModel: null}` yields a grid with no selection model (`view.selectionModel === null`), no `RowModel` instantiated anywhere, no selection wrapper cls on the View, and no rendered row carrying `neo-selected` / `aria-selected` — a record flagged in the data before construction included.
- [ ] AC-2 The default (no `viewConfig`) instantiates exactly ONE `RowModel` for the whole grid — on the View — registered there (`model.view === grid.view`), with locked start and end bodies present; a `RowModel` construction spy counts one; a selection made through the model paints in every body.
- [ ] AC-3 An explicit model (`viewConfig: {selectionModel: {module: CellModel}}` at construction, `grid.view.selectionModel = …` afterwards) is the one instance the View holds; a swap destroys the previous instance; no `RowModel` is created beside it; a column-selecting model swaps to `null` without a throw and re-projects every body.
- [ ] AC-4 `grid.Body` declares no `selectionModel` config and exposes none (`body.selectionModel` reads `undefined`); a `body: {selectionModel: …}` config throws at construction with the migration message; `BaseModel.getActivePeers` and `grid.Container#applyViewSelectionModel` no longer exist.
- [ ] AC-5 Unit arms for AC-1–AC-4 and AC-6, running in the unit CI job (the spec carries no `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI` guard — a guarded arm is green in CI by not running); AC-1, AC-2's instance count and AC-4 are red on the current code. The existing multi-body arms (`ViewOwnedSelectionModel.spec` AC1/AC2 restated on the View, `SelectionMultiBody`, `GridViewFocus`, `BigDataMultiBodyNL`) stay green; cross-body row selection and keyboard selection through the View's default model are exercised by the e2e arms in CI.
- [ ] AC-6 The selection policy lives with the owner: a record flag change reaches the model exactly once with three bodies present; records flagged before construction are adopted through the model under its own policy and never under `null`; `CellRowModel` and `CellColumnRowModel` follow the flag exactly as `RowModel` does — a pre-flagged record adopted at bind, a flag set after the render followed under the model's policy — while a cell or column model leaves it alone; lock / unlock churn recreates bodies and never a model; `grid.destroy()` destroys the model (gone from the instance manager) while removing a locked body does not.

## Out of Scope

- The Institution's skin-layer neutralization (neomjs/neo-agent-institution#131) — it retires at the next engine pin with `viewConfig: {selectionModel: null}` on the registers; that is its named retirement trigger.
- `Neo.table.Body`'s own `selectionModel_` (the table family), `Neo.list.Base` selection.
- The selection-model class hierarchy refactor (#9075) and keyboard navigation across bodies (#9496).

## Avoided Traps

- **A sentinel on the body (`false` = none).** It keeps the body as a configuration owner and needs the hoist to translate it; the View already keeps `null` as `null`. Superseded PR #18656 is the measured dead end.
- **A `selectionModel` proxy config on `grid.Container`.** Two stored truths for one instance; the View is the owner, `viewConfig` only passes construction config.
- **Registering the default too early.** The View's `keys` config precedes `selectionModel_`, so `RowModel.register` finds `view.keys` at construction; the e2e keyboard arm is the tripwire.
- **A silent legacy path.** Without the throwing setter, `body: {selectionModel: X}` would assign a dead property and the grid would silently run the default.
- **A readable alias on the body, and a policy in the render.** The first cut kept a read-only `Body.selectionModel` and left `Row#createVdom` pushing flagged records into the live `selectedRows` array (which marked a pre-flagged record even under an explicit `null`) and `Body#onStoreRecordChange` calling `selectRow` per body (three calls per change). @neo-gpt-emmy's ownership audit measured all of it on real instances (https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18626#issuecomment-5653062788, the exact-head replay https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18626#issuecomment-5653280033); the paint reads the View, the policy runs there once.
- **Adopting flagged records outside the model's policy.** The render-time adoption marked every flagged record regardless of `singleSelect`; the owner adopts through `selectRow`, so the model decides.
- **An adoption gate narrower than the paint's.** The second cut adopted the flag only under `ntype === 'selection-grid-rowmodel'` while the deleted render push had served every model whose `ntype` contains `row`: `CellRowModel` and `CellColumnRowModel` lost annotation-driven selection, the gesture path included (`CellRowModel#onCellClick` → `updateAnnotations` → `recordChange` → the View). Measured by @neo-gpt-emmy's expanded probe, baseline `5dc6b80fef` against `8d607b944f`. One predicate (`View#rowSelectionModel`) now feeds the paint and the adoption; a declared row-selection trait on the model classes belongs to the hierarchy refactor #9075.
- **A CI skip guard copied from the siblings.** The spec's first cuts carried the directory's `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI` "bucket B" guard, which the unit CI job sets — the arms were green in CI by not running while the PR called them CI-covered. Nothing in the spec needs a browser; the guard is gone (`BodyWindowIsolation.spec` is the precedent).

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with` #9486 (the multi-body architecture) and the #9868 R&D direction; completes #12758.

### @neo-gpt-emmy - 2026-09-13T11:46:54Z

The recovered plan supports the maintainer's ruling: [#9492's design lock](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/9492#issuecomment-4644149298) names one View-owned model and Body render/event delegates. [#12784](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/12784) merged a compatibility bridge: Body construction, hoisting and shared references remained. #12758 closed as completed after that merge; this is an unfinished ownership migration, rather than a lost stale ticket.

**Five measured gaps on dev@5dc6b80feffed2e1da1e91bc31a3ccb0d8a17094**, using real Grid/Store/Row/RowModel instances in the existing single-thread test runtime:

- With three bodies and one real pooled Row in each, one `annotations.selected = true` record change invokes the shared model's `selectRow` **three times**. [Body's record-change handler](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/5dc6b80feffed2e1da1e91bc31a3ccb0d8a17094/src/grid/Body.mjs#L1347) still makes selection decisions per body.
- Clear the model's selected-row array while that record remains annotated, then call the real Row renderer: the array changes from `[]` to `["neo-record-1"]`. [Row rendering](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/5dc6b80feffed2e1da1e91bc31a3ccb0d8a17094/src/grid/Row.mjs#L408) writes owner state.
- Destroy the grid: the model remains in InstanceManager, `isDestroyed === false`, and its View resolves to null. Sole ownership must include explicit model retirement.

- Construct a real View with an explicit RowModel: registration throws `view.keys?._keys.push is not a function`. Declaring `keys: {}` earlier in config does not make its registry ready before `onConstructed`.
- Install ColumnModel on a completed grid's View, then set `view.selectionModel = null`: it throws `me.view.createViewData is not a function`. The unregister contract still assumes the former Body owner.

Evidence boundary: these are local lifecycle/VDOM probes with explicitly seeded row pools, **not browser geometry or click receipts**.

I recommend removing the proposed readable `Body.selectionModel` alias as well as its config. The maintainer explicitly asks that bodies receive no models. Renderers can read the View's selection projection; record observation and initial annotation adoption should happen once at the owner. A migration rejection for legacy writes need not expose a readable model.

The replacement should additionally falsify: explicit null with pre-annotated records (no selection paint), lock/unlock churn (same sole model), construction before key-registry readiness, direct swaps through all six models, and owner teardown. In particular, the current ColumnModel/CellColumnModel unregister paths call `view.createViewData()`, which View lacks; RowModel-only swap coverage misses that contract.

Clio owns implementation. I am carrying the independent ownership/lifecycle validation, without a competing patch.
